note: Declared before judging. Every expectation is a band or a contract-declared value from docs/planning/m2-contracts/physics.md §7/§8 and the frozen packet-14 course tolerances (tests/evaluations/m2-physics/course-spec.json). The measured values are recorded in docs/acceptance/evidence-m2/31/, never used to set a band. Slope cases declare a 1-step settle because the 0.20.0 controller only registers ground contact after a first downward probe (measured, C31-2/C31-4).

driver.model: packet-14 canonical character model (probe-rapier2d.mjs): grounded && !airborne => vy = 0; jump edge while grounded => vy = jumpVelocity, airborne = true; otherwise vy += gravity_y*dt clamped to maxFallSpeed; airborne clears when grounded && vy <= 0. The controller module itself is packet 32.
driver.delta: { x: moveX * speed * dt, y: vy * dt }, dt = 1/120

cases.description: Capsule resting on the frozen flat floor: grounded every step, rest center 0.910 m ± 0.0005, support normal (0, 1).
Walk right from x=-10 over the floor seam at x=0 at 4 m/s: grounded except at most two steps, speed inside the 5 % band, no penetration.
Run right into the wall face at x=9.5: the capsule stops within face + reach + skin + 5 mm, reports a wall contact, never penetrates.

expect.maxXNote: wall face x=9.5; the capsule radius is 0.3 and the controller skin 0.01, so the center must stop by 9.195 (contract wall stop band 0.05 m)

cases.description: Approach the same wall at 12 m/s (0.1 m/step): no tunnelling beyond the 5 mm penetration budget and a wall contact is observed.

expect.maxXNote: wall face x=9.5; the capsule radius is 0.3 and the controller skin 0.01, so the center must stop by 9.195 (contract wall stop band 0.05 m)

cases.description: Climb the 43° ramp to its top corner, then jump straight up under the ceiling (underside y=4.0): a head contact is reported, the center never passes 3.095 + tolerance and the rise after the contact step stays at the controller nudge scale.

maxStepRiseAfterContact.note: physics.md §7: the realized rise after the head-contact step must stay at the controller nudge scale (5e-4 m per step)

cases.description: Climb the 43° ramp (below the 45° climb limit) from x=1.5: grounded for at least 95 % of the ascent, the center exits near the authored top-corner offset (3.579, 2.703) ± 0.5 m, no penetration below the floor.
Push into the 47° ramp (above the 45° climb limit) for 1 s: height gain stays below 0.3 m (the character does not climb a too-steep slope).
Climb a bounded convex-polygon ramp (4-vertex CCW hull, about 35°) created through ColliderDesc.convexHull: grounded, the center rises along the polygon face.
Climb a bounded convex-polygon ramp (4-vertex CCW hull, exactly 45°, at the climb limit): grounded, the center rises along the polygon face.
Run into the convex-polygon wall: blocked without penetration and with a wall contact reported.
Walk off a 0.05 m step down (inside the 0.1 m snap distance): the capsule stays grounded (at most the transition step ungrounded) and snap is reported at least once.
Walk off a 0.50 m drop (beyond the 0.1 m snap distance): the character free-falls (at least five ungrounded steps), never reports snapped while ungrounded, and lands.
pins: contract-change request C31-3 (snap chaining over a bridged drop)

cases.description: Standing on a 29.9° ramp face: the adapter reports the library's raw grounded flag (physics.md §8 item 1) and the support normal of the face; steepSlope=false marks the climbable decision the controller applies (§8 items 2/4).
cases.startNote: capsule center placed at along-slope s=1.0 + the upright-capsule support offset (0.6*cos(angle) + 0.3) + the 0.1 m box half-thickness along the face normal; the declared 1-step settle establishes the ground contact (the contact is only registered after the first downward probe — measured).

cases.description: Standing on a 30.0° face with no input for 1 s: the measured 0.20.0 behavior is that the controller does NOT slide the character down by itself (vertical loss stays below 0.01 m), although physics.md §7/§8 describe 30.0° as the minimum slide angle. Recorded as C31-4; the slide/traversal policy belongs to the packet-32 controller.
